what_it_does: Edge workstations — compact computers used at remote sites — often need to pull large files from distant cloud storage servers. The usual way to do this relies on a complex chain of software running on the workstation's main processor (CPU), and that software chain is too slow to keep the storage connection fully busy, wasting about 75% of its potential speed. Leopard is a custom hardware controller built onto a SmartNIC (a network card with its own programmable chip, here an FPGA — a chip whose logic can be rewired in software) that takes over the storage access job entirely. Instead of the CPU managing each storage request step by step, Leopard's hardware circuits handle many requests in parallel and send them directly over the network to the remote server, bypassing the slow software layers. The result is that the full speed of the NVMe storage protocol (a fast standard for talking to solid-state drives) is available to edge devices without taxing the CPU.
